extensive perineural and intraneural invasion

concepts.why: The patient's history of a recurring forehead lesion with a Breslow thickness of 6 mm, 14 mitotic figures/mm2, and extensive perineural and intraneural invasion, combined with the presence of a left superior orbit mass and intense enhancement of the V1 branch of the left frontal nerve, supports the diagnosis of Malignant Melanoma of the Orbit.

rationales.F01: Diplopia and pain suggest orbital involvement, which is consistent with both Malignant Melanoma of the Orbit and Metastatic Melanoma to the Orbit.
rationales.F03: A Breslow thickness of 6 mm is a significant indicator of malignant melanoma, supporting both concepts.
rationales.F04: High mitotic figures/mm2 indicate aggressive tumor behavior, supporting both Malignant Melanoma of the Orbit and Metastatic Melanoma to the Orbit.
rationales.F06: Extensive perineural and intraneural invasion is a characteristic feature of malignant melanoma, particularly supporting Malignant Melanoma of the Orbit.
rationales.F11: The presence of a left superior orbit mass extending along the supraorbital nerve to the cavernous sinus with indistinct borders and fat stranding is highly suggestive of malignant melanoma, supporting both concepts.
rationales.F12: Intense enhancement of the V1 branch of the left frontal nerve with associated fat stranding is indicative of tumor involvement, supporting both Malignant Melanoma of the Orbit and Metastatic Melanoma to the Orbit.
